questions.q: How is the number 40,07,060 read in the Indian system?
questions.a: forty lakh seven thousand sixty

questions.q: A school library app shows the pages read by all its students in a year as 63052418, without commas. Which shows the commas placed correctly in the Indian system?
(a) Write 'eighty two lakh four thousand nine' in figures, with commas in the Indian system. (b) How many digits does this number have?
questions.a: (a) 82,04,009 (b) It has 7 digits.
s: Writes 82,04,009 with commas in the 3-2-2 pattern
States that the number has 7 digits

questions.q: The digit 5 appears four times in 5,25,05,500. (a) Write the number in words in the Indian system. (b) Write the place value of each of the four 5s. (c) How many times the place value of the rightmost 5 is the place value of the leftmost 5?
questions.a: (a) Five crore twenty five lakh five thousand five hundred. (b) The 5s stand for 5,00,00,000 (5 crore), 5,00,000 (5 lakh), 5,000 (5 thousand) and 500 (5 hundred). (c) 5,00,00,000 / 500 = 1,00,000, so it is one lakh times.
s: Writes the number name: five crore twenty five lakh five thousand five hundred
Gives the four place values 5 crore, 5 lakh, 5 thousand and 500
Divides 5,00,00,000 by 500 to get 1,00,000 (one lakh) times

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The number 10,00,000 has one digit more than 9,99,999.
Reason (R): Ten lakh is the smallest 7-digit number, and 9,99,999 is the largest 6-digit number.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
A district education office in Mysuru orders textbooks for three blocks. Block A needs 12,40,500 books, Block B needs 9,85,250 books and Block C needs 4,07,075 books. The printing press gives a lower rate on any single order of at least ten lakh books. The office must also write every figure in words in its order letter.
(a) Write the number of books for Block C in words in the Indian system.
(b) Which of the three blocks, ordering on its own, gets the lower rate?
(c) Find the total number of books for all three blocks, with Indian commas.
(d) The office plans to send Block B and Block C as one combined order. Should it do so? Justify with numbers.
questions.a: (a) Four lakh seven thousand seventy five. (b) Only Block A, since 12,40,500 is at least 10,00,000 while 9,85,250 and 4,07,075 are below ten lakh. (c) 12,40,500 + 9,85,250 + 4,07,075 = 26,32,825 books. (d) Yes: the combined order is 9,85,250 + 4,07,075 = 13,92,325, which is 3,92,325 more than ten lakh, so the books for B and C also get the lower rate.
s: (a) Writes four lakh seven thousand seventy five
(b) Names Block A only, comparing each figure with 10,00,000
(d) Finds 13,92,325, compares with ten lakh and decides yes

questions.q: In the American system, what is the name of the number written in the Indian system as 10,00,000 (ten lakh)?
questions.a: One million

questions.q:
Match each number in Column I (Indian system) with its name in Column II (American system).
Column I: I. 1,00,000  II. 10,00,000  III. 1,00,00,000  IV. 1,00,00,00,000
Column II: A. One billion  B. Ten million  C. Hundred thousand  D. One million
questions.a: I-C, II-D, III-B, IV-A

questions.q: True or false: 80 crore is more than one billion. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. One billion is one arab, which is 100 crore. 80 crore is 800 million, which is less than one billion (1,000 million).
s: Gives the reason: 1 billion = 100 crore, and 80 crore (800 million) is less

questions.q: A London newspaper says that a film earned 'thirty five million four hundred thousand rupees'. (a) Write this amount in figures with American commas. (b) Write the same amount with Indian commas and read it in the Indian system.
questions.a: (a) 35,400,000 (b) 3,54,00,000, read as three crore fifty four lakh rupees.
s: Writes 35,400,000 with commas in the 3-3-3 pattern
Rewrites it as 3,54,00,000 and reads it as three crore fifty four lakh

questions.q:
Three companies report their yearly income in different ways. Company P: ₹7,08,40,000 (Indian commas). Company Q: ₹70,084,000 (American commas). Company R: 'seven crore eighty four lakh rupees'.
(a) Rewrite Q's income with Indian commas and give its Indian name.
(b) Give the American name of P's income.
(c) Write R's income in figures with American commas.
(d) Arrange the three incomes from smallest to largest.
(e) How much more does R earn than Q? Give the answer in lakh and thousand.
questions.a: (a) 7,00,84,000: seven crore eighty four thousand. (b) 70,840,000: seventy million eight hundred forty thousand. (c) 78,400,000. (d) Q (7,00,84,000) < P (7,08,40,000) < R (7,84,00,000). (e) 7,84,00,000 - 7,00,84,000 = 83,16,000, that is 83 lakh 16 thousand rupees.
s: (a) Writes 7,00,84,000 and names it seven crore eighty four thousand
(b) Names P as seventy million eight hundred forty thousand
(d) Orders them Q, P, R after comparing in one system

questions.q:
Consider the following statements.
I. 100 million is the same as one crore.
II. In the American system, digits are grouped in threes from the right (3-3-3).
III. 1,00,00,00,000 has as many zeros as one billion.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: II and III only

questions.q: Systematic Sippy has the buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000, +10000 and +100000, and always uses as few clicks as possible. How many clicks does it need to show 3,042?
Thoughtful Thousands has only a +1000 button. (a) How many times must it be pressed to show 64,000? (b) What number does it show after 210 presses? Write it with Indian commas.

Creative Chitti has the buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000 and +10000. Find the number it shows for each set of clicks. (a) (6 x 1000) + (4 x 100) + (5 x 1) (b) (23 x 100) + (7 x 10) (c) (12 x 1000) + (15 x 10)
A calculator has the buttons +1, +10, +100 and +1000. Which set of clicks does NOT show 8,060?

A shop's billing counter has the buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000, +10000 and +100000. The cashier must show ₹2,03,450. (a) Write the expression that uses the fewest clicks and count the clicks. (b) The +100000 button stops working. Write the expression with the fewest clicks now and count them. (c) The +10000 button also stops working. Write the expression with the fewest clicks and count them. (d) How many more clicks does (c) need than (a)?
s: (a) Writes the place-value expression and counts 14 clicks
(b) Replaces 2 lakh by 20 ten-thousands and counts 32 clicks

questions.q:
At a science fair in Bhopal, each stall shows its token count on an old counter with the buttons +1, +10, +100, +1000 and +10000. Every click takes one second, and each stall uses as few clicks as possible. Stall A must show 47,305 tokens, Stall B must show 9,999 tokens and Stall C must show 60,060 tokens. The organiser gives a prize to the stall that shows its number in the shortest time.
(a) How many clicks does Stall A need?
(b) How many clicks does Stall B need?
(c) How many clicks does Stall C need?
(d) Stall B's owner says, 'My number is the smallest, so I will surely win.' Is he right? Which stall wins, and what decides the number of clicks?
questions.a: (a) 4 + 7 + 3 + 0 + 5 = 19 clicks. (b) 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36 clicks. (c) 6 + 0 + 0 + 6 + 0 = 12 clicks. (d) No. Stall B needs the most clicks (36), and Stall C wins with 12 clicks. With the fewest clicks, the number of clicks is the sum of the digits, not the size of the number.
s: (d) Says B is wrong, names Stall C, and explains that the clicks equal the digit sum

questions.q: What is the nearest thousand of 4,36,718?

Assertion (A): A school with 1,265 students and staff should order about 1,300 snacks for a picnic rather than about 1,200.
Reason (R): When an approximate number must not fall short of the actual number, we round up.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: Round 58,46,291 to (a) the nearest lakh (b) the nearest ten lakh.
s: (a) 58,00,000, since 46,291 is less than half a lakh
(b) 60,00,000, since 58,46,291 is nearer to 60 lakh than to 50 lakh

questions.q: Anu says: 'If two numbers have the same nearest lakh, they must also have the same nearest thousand.' Test her claim with 3,41,200 and 3,38,900 and give your verdict.
questions.a: Both numbers have the nearest lakh 3,00,000. But the nearest thousand of 3,41,200 is 3,41,000 and that of 3,38,900 is 3,39,000. These are different, so Anu's claim is false.
s: Finds the nearest lakh of both numbers: 3,00,000
Concludes that the claim is false, with this example as proof

questions.q: Decide in each case whether to round up or round down, and give the rounded value. (a) A stadium expects 87,350 fans and prints entry passes in bundles of 10,000; every fan must get a pass. How many passes should it print? (b) A club has ₹4,72,600 and buys sports kits sold only in lots worth ₹10,000 each; it must not spend more than it has. How much can it spend on kits? (c) How many passes are left over in (a), and how much money is left unspent in (b)? (d) The club pays a builder exactly ₹4,72,600 by cheque. Should the cheque be rounded? Give a reason.
questions.a: (a) Round up: 90,000 passes (9 bundles), because 80,000 would leave fans without passes. (b) Round down: ₹4,70,000 (47 lots), because ₹4,80,000 is more than it has. (c) 90,000 - 87,350 = 2,650 spare passes; ₹4,72,600 - ₹4,70,000 = ₹2,600 unspent. (d) No. A payment must be the exact amount, so it is not rounded.
s: (a) Rounds up to 90,000 passes with the reason
(b) Rounds down to ₹4,70,000 with the reason
(d) Says the payment must be exact and is not rounded

questions.q:
A newspaper in Nagpur reports the visitors to a four-day book fair: Day 1 had 38,472 visitors, Day 2 had 41,905, Day 3 had 56,218 and Day 4 had 63,540. The editor wants rounded figures for the headlines. The organiser hires chairs in sets of 1,000 and wants a chair for every visitor on the busiest day.
(a) On which day did the most people visit?
(b) Round the Day 1 figure to the nearest thousand.
(c) Round the Day 3 figure to the nearest ten thousand.
(d) How many chairs should the organiser hire? Should the busiest day's figure be rounded up or down for this?
questions.a: (a) Day 4 (63,540). (b) 38,000. (c) 60,000. (d) Round up: 64,000 chairs (64 sets), because rounding down to 63,000 would leave 540 visitors without a chair.
s: (d) Rounds up to 64,000 chairs and says why

questions.q: Without adding exactly, which is the best estimate of 2,98,700 + 5,03,100?

Consider the following statements.
I. 3,10,000 + 4,20,000 is more than 7,00,000.
II. 8,90,000 - 2,05,000 is less than 6,00,000.
III. 4,60,000 and 3,70,000 are each more than 3,50,000, so their sum is more than 7,00,000.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and III only

questions.q: (a) Round 6,72,400 and 2,18,900 to the nearest lakh and use them to estimate their sum. (b) Find the exact sum.

Is 15,28,400 - 6,61,700 more than or less than 9,00,000? (a) Decide without subtracting in full, by comparing each number with a nearby round number. (b) State your conclusion. (c) Find the exact difference to check.
questions.a: (a) 15,28,400 is less than 15,30,000 and 6,61,700 is more than 6,60,000, so the difference is less than 15,30,000 - 6,60,000 = 8,70,000. (b) So the difference is less than 9,00,000. (c) 15,28,400 - 6,61,700 = 8,66,700, which is less than 9,00,000.
s: (b) Concludes the difference is less than 9,00,000

questions.q:
A village panchayat has ₹25,00,000 for the year. It plans four works: a road (₹8,64,500), a well (₹3,92,800), a school room (₹7,46,300) and solar lights (₹4,18,600).
(a) Round each cost to the nearest lakh and estimate the total.
(b) Is the estimate more or less than the money available, and by how much?
(c) Explain why the panchayat should not decide only from this estimate.
(d) Find the exact total cost.
(e) Can all four works be done? How much money is left or short?
questions.a: (a) 9 + 4 + 7 + 4 = 24 lakh, so about ₹24,00,000. (b) Less, by about ₹1,00,000. (c) Rounding to the nearest lakh can change each cost by up to ₹50,000, and here the estimate is only one lakh below the budget, so the rounding errors could change the answer; the exact total is needed. (d) 8,64,500 + 3,92,800 + 7,46,300 + 4,18,600 = ₹24,22,200. (e) Yes. ₹25,00,000 - ₹24,22,200 = ₹77,800 is left.
s: (a) Rounds to 9, 4, 7 and 4 lakh and estimates ₹24,00,000
(b) Says the estimate is about ₹1,00,000 less than the budget
(c) Explains that rounding errors of up to half a lakh each could change the decision

questions.q: Roxie rounds both numbers in 7,48,000 + 2,46,000 to the nearest lakh and gets an estimate of 9,00,000. Which statement about the exact sum is correct?
questions.a: It is nearer 10,00,000, as both numbers were rounded down by almost half a lakh.
o: It is nearer 10,00,000, as both numbers were rounded down by almost half a lakh.
It equals 9,00,000, as rounding to the nearest lakh does not change a sum.
It is less than 9,00,000, as both numbers were rounded down to whole lakhs.
It is about 9,50,000, as the two rounding errors cancel each other out.

questions.q: Using 'multiplying by 5 is the same as multiplying by 10 and halving', find 348 x 5.

Work out each product in Column I using a shortcut and match it with its value in Column II.
Column I: I. 36 x 25  II. 48 x 125  III. 64 x 5  IV. 26 x 50
Column II: A. 6,000  B. 1,300  C. 900  D. 320
questions.a: I-C, II-A, III-D, IV-B

questions.q: True or false: 96 x 25 = 2,400, because 96 x 25 is the same as 96 x 100 divided by 4. Give the reason or the correct statement.
Find each product quickly by regrouping the factors. Show the grouping you use. (a) 2 x 637 x 50 (b) 4 x 89 x 25 (c) 8 x 213 x 125 (d) 250 x 16 (e) 5 x 46 x 20
s: (d) Splits 16 = 4 x 4, uses 250 x 4 = 1000 and gets 4,000

questions.q:
A sweet shop in Coimbatore packs 25 laddus in every box. During the festival week it filled 1,264 boxes and sold each box for ₹125. The owner wants quick totals without long multiplication, so he uses the shortcuts 25 = 100 / 4 and 125 = 1000 / 8.
(a) How many laddus were packed in all?
(b) How much money did the shop get for all the boxes?
(c) If the same laddus had been packed 50 to a box, how many boxes would be needed?
(d) His son suggests selling 50-laddu boxes at ₹250 each. Would the shop earn more, less or the same? Show why.
questions.a: (a) 1,264 x 25 = 1,26,400 / 4 = 31,600 laddus. (b) 1,264 x 125 = 12,64,000 / 8 = ₹1,58,000. (c) 31,600 / 50 = 632 boxes. (d) 632 x 250 = 6,32,000 / 4 = ₹1,58,000, the same as before, because twice the laddus at twice the price gives the same total.
s: (d) Finds ₹1,58,000 and concludes the earning is the same

questions.q: How many digits can the product of a 3-digit number and a 2-digit number have?
questions.a: 4 or 5

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The product of a 4-digit number and a 1-digit number can have just 4 digits.
Reason (R): The product of an m-digit number and an n-digit number always has exactly m + n digits.
questions.a: A is true but R is false.
o: A is true but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q: (a) Find 9,999 x 99 and 1,000 x 10, and count the digits in each product. (b) Use these to state how many digits the product of any 4-digit number and any 2-digit number can have.
questions.a: (a) 9,999 x 99 = 9,89,901 (6 digits); 1,000 x 10 = 10,000 (5 digits). (b) These are the largest and smallest such products, so the product has 5 or 6 digits.
s: (b) Concludes 5 or 6 digits, as these are the largest and smallest products

questions.q: Kavya multiplies a 3-digit number by another 3-digit number and then multiplies the result by 10. She says, 'My final answer can have 5 digits.' Check her claim using the smallest and largest possible answers.
questions.a: Smallest: 100 x 100 x 10 = 1,00,000, which has 6 digits. Largest: 999 x 999 x 10 = 99,80,010, which has 7 digits. So the answer has 6 or 7 digits and can never have 5 digits; Kavya is wrong.
s: Concludes 6 or 7 digits, so the claim is false

questions.q: Without multiplying, write the two possible numbers of digits in each product. Use the rule that an m-digit number times an n-digit number has m + n - 1 or m + n digits. (a) a 1-digit number x a 4-digit number (b) a 4-digit number x a 4-digit number (c) a 5-digit number x a 2-digit number (d) a 6-digit number x a 3-digit number
questions.a: (a) 4 or 5 digits (b) 7 or 8 digits (c) 6 or 7 digits (d) 8 or 9 digits

questions.q: Which pair of numbers can NEVER have a 6-digit product?
questions.a: a 2-digit number and a 3-digit number

questions.q: A cyclist rides 50 km every day. How far does she ride in a year of 365 days?
A school kitchen uses 120 eggs every working day. (a) How many eggs does it use in 30 working days? (b) How many does it use in a year of 250 working days?

A ship like the RMS Titanic carried about 2,500 passengers. In 2011 the population of Bhopal was 17,98,218. (a) How many people can 500 such ships carry? (b) Can the whole population of Bhopal fit into 500 such ships? (c) What is the smallest number of such ships that can carry all of them?
questions.a: (a) 500 x 2,500 = 12,50,000 people. (b) No, because 17,98,218 is more than 12,50,000. (c) 17,98,218 / 2,500 is about 719.3, so 719 ships are not enough and 720 ships are needed.
s: (c) Divides and rounds up to 720 ships

questions.q:
A grey-headed albatross can fly about 900 to 1,000 km in a day, and one of its longest recorded trips was about 12,000 km. A bar-tailed godwit flew 13,560 km without stopping in about 11 days.
(a) How many days does the 12,000 km trip take at 1,000 km a day?
(b) How many days does it take at 900 km a day? Is 13 days enough?
(c) About how many km did the godwit cover each day?
(d) About how many km did it cover each hour?
(e) Which bird covers more distance in a day? Use your answers to decide.
questions.a: (a) 12,000 / 1,000 = 12 days. (b) 13 days give 13 x 900 = 11,700 km, which is short of 12,000 km, so 13 days are not enough; it takes about 14 days. (c) 13,560 / 11 is about 1,233 km a day. (d) 1,233 / 24 is about 51 km an hour. (e) The godwit, about 1,233 km a day, which is more than the albatross's 900 to 1,000 km a day.
s: (b) Shows 13 x 900 = 11,700 is short and gives about 14 days
(e) Decides the godwit covers more per day, comparing 1,233 with 900 to 1,000

questions.q:
A school in Indore collects old notebooks for recycling. It has 1,200 students, and each student brings 4 old notebooks with 80 sheets in each. Take each sheet to weigh 5 grams (1 kg = 1,000 grams). A recycling van can carry at most 1,500 kg in one trip, and the recycler pays ₹12 for every kg of paper. A second van trip costs the school ₹900.
(a) How many sheets are collected in all?
(b) What is their total weight in kg?
(c) Can one van trip carry all the paper?
(d) Should the school pay for a second trip or leave the extra paper behind? Justify with money.
questions.a: (a) 1,200 x 4 x 80 = 3,84,000 sheets. (b) 3,84,000 x 5 = 19,20,000 g = 1,920 kg. (c) No; 1,920 kg is 420 kg more than 1,500 kg. (d) The extra 420 kg earns 420 x ₹12 = ₹5,040, which is more than the ₹900 trip cost, so the school should pay for the second trip (it gains ₹4,140 more).
s: (d) Compares ₹5,040 with ₹900 and decides to pay for the second trip

questions.q:
Consider the following statements (take 1 day = 24 hours, 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 year = 365 days).
I. Counting one coin every second without stopping, it takes more than 10 days to count 10,00,000 coins.
II. A tap that drips 30 drops every minute drips more than 40,000 drops in a day.
III. Travelling 100 km every day, a person covers 3,84,400 km in 10 years.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.a: I and II only

questions.q: When one crore is written in figures, how many zeros does it have?

Assertion (A): One arab is the same as 100 crore.
Reason (R): One crore is the same as 100 lakh.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

questions.q:
Work out each product in Column I and match it with its value in Column II.
Column I: I. 40 lakh x 5  II. 25 thousand x 400  III. 2 crore x 50  IV. 6 lakh x 50
Column II: A. 1 arab  B. 3 crore  C. 2 crore  D. 1 crore
questions.a: I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-B

questions.q: True or false: a thousand lakh is the same as one crore. Give the reason or the correct statement.
questions.a: False. One crore is 100 lakh. A thousand lakh is 1,00,000 x 1,000 = 10,00,00,000, which is 10 crore (1 followed by 8 zeros).
s: Corrects it: 100 lakh = 1 crore, so a thousand lakh = 10 crore

questions.q: A library has 1,00,000 books. A keen reader finishes 2 books every week. Take a year to be 52 weeks. (a) How many books does she read in a year? (b) How many does she read in 80 years? (c) At least how many such readers, sharing the books with no repeats, are needed to read all one lakh books in 80 years?
questions.a: (a) 2 x 52 = 104 books. (b) 104 x 80 = 8,320 books. (c) 12 readers read 12 x 8,320 = 99,840, which is short of 1,00,000, so at least 13 readers are needed.
s: (c) Shows 12 readers fall short (99,840) and gives 13

questions.q:
If 1 lakh people stood shoulder to shoulder in a line, they could stretch about 38 km. A city has an outer ring road that is 152 km long, and about 18 lakh people live in the city.
(a) How long would a line of 5 lakh people be?
(b) How many lakh people are needed to make a line once around the whole ring road?
(c) If all the people of the city stood in such a line along the ring road, how many full rounds could they make?
(d) How many people would be left over after those full rounds?
(e) How long would the line of the people left over be, and what part of the ring road would it cover?
questions.a: (a) 5 x 38 = 190 km. (b) 152 / 38 = 4, so 4 lakh people. (c) 18 lakh / 4 lakh = 4.5, so 4 full rounds. (d) 4 full rounds use 16 lakh people, so 18 lakh - 16 lakh = 2 lakh people are left over. (e) 2 x 38 = 76 km, which is half of the 152 km ring road.

questions.q: Using each of the digits 3, 8, 1 and 6 exactly once, what is the largest 4-digit number you can make?
Using each of the digits 2, 0, 7, 5 and 9 exactly once (the first digit cannot be 0), what is the smallest 5-digit even number?

The digits need these numbers of sticks: 0 needs 6, 1 needs 2, 2 needs 5, 3 needs 5, 4 needs 4, 5 needs 5, 6 needs 6, 7 needs 3, 8 needs 7, 9 needs 6. (a) How many sticks are needed to write 3,965? (b) Which needs more sticks, 3,965 or 8,008?
questions.a: (a) 5 + 6 + 6 + 5 = 22 sticks. (b) 8,008 needs 7 + 6 + 6 + 7 = 26 sticks, so 8,008 needs more.

questions.q: Use each of the digits 4, 0, 7, 2 and 5 exactly once to make a 5-digit number (the first digit cannot be 0). (a) Write the largest such number that is a multiple of 5. (b) Write the smallest such number that is a multiple of 5.
questions.a: (a) 75,420 (it must end in 0 or 5; ending in 0 gives 75,420, which beats 74,205). (b) 20,475 (ending in 5 lets 0 stay in the second place; ending in 0 gives only 24,570).

questions.q: The digits need these numbers of sticks: 0 needs 6, 1 needs 2, 2 needs 5, 3 needs 5, 4 needs 4, 5 needs 5, 6 needs 6, 7 needs 3, 8 needs 7, 9 needs 6. (a) How many sticks are needed for 2,580? (b) How many sticks are needed for 9,999? (c) Which single digit needs the most sticks?
questions.a: (a) 5 + 5 + 7 + 6 = 23 sticks (b) 4 x 6 = 24 sticks (c) 8, which needs 7 sticks

questions.q: The digits need these numbers of sticks: 0 needs 6, 1 needs 2, 2 needs 5, 3 needs 5, 4 needs 4, 5 needs 5, 6 needs 6, 7 needs 3, 8 needs 7, 9 needs 6. Every number below must use exactly 20 sticks. (a) Find the largest 4-digit number. (b) Find the smallest 4-digit number. (c) Explain why no 2-digit number can use exactly 20 sticks. (d) Find the largest 5-digit number.
questions.a: (a) 9,991: start with as many 9s as possible; 9 + 9 + 9 uses 18 sticks, and the last 2 sticks make a 1 (6 + 6 + 6 + 2 = 20). (b) 1,000: 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 2 + 6 + 6 + 6 = 20 sticks. (c) The most sticks any digit needs is 7 (the digit 8), so two digits need at most 14 sticks. (d) 99,771: two 9s use 12 sticks, leaving 8 sticks for three digits; the third digit can use at most 4 sticks (the last two need at least 2 each), so the largest choice is 7 (3 sticks), and the last 5 sticks make 7 and 1 (6 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 20).
s: (c) Two digits need at most 7 + 7 = 14 sticks
(d) 99,771 with a stick check and reason
